title: Is it my preference? Role Grounding Attack against Agent's Memory via Social Interaction
abstract: arXiv:2610.38209v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM-based agents now share experiences on social platforms and remember new preferences to enhance their performance. However, existing memory systems contain a vulnerability in role-to-principal attribution that attackers can exploit. We identify Role Grounding Misattribution, in which an attacker-designed interaction causes the victim agent to incorrectly record a preference from the attacker as a preference of the victim's user. Specifically, we are the first to formalize Role Grounding Attack (RGA), an attack model that exploits this vulnerability through nested conversation structures. In the memory formation stage, an experience-sharing post quoting a conversation between the attacker agent and its user is published, which explicitly identifies its publisher. translated_title: 这是我的偏好吗？通过社交互动对智能体记忆发起的角色定位攻击
translated_abstract: 摘要：基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体如今在社交平台上分享经验，并记住新的偏好以提升自身性能。然而，现有记忆系统在角色与主体归属（role-to-principal attribution）方面存在一个可被攻击者利用的漏洞。我们识别出“角色定位误归属”（Role Grounding Misattribution）现象，即攻击者设计的交互会导致受害智能体错误地将攻击者的偏好记录为受害智能体所属用户的偏好。具体而言，我们首次正式化定义了角色定位攻击（Role Grounding Attack, RGA），这是一种利用嵌套对话结构来触发该漏洞的攻击模型。在记忆形成阶段，攻击者发布一篇经验分享帖子，其中引用了攻击者智能体与其用户之间的对话，且该帖子明确标识了发布者身份。内部对话表达了攻击者智能体所属用户的偏好。当受害智能体从这个嵌套结构中记忆偏好时，其记忆失去了……
tldr: 首次正式定义了角色定位攻击（RGA），揭示攻击者可通过社交平台上的嵌套对话结构，使受害LLM智能体将攻击者的偏好错误地记入其用户的记忆中。
en_tdlr: This paper is the first to formalize the Role Grounding Attack (RGA), showing that attackers can exploit nested conversation structures on social platforms to make a victim LLM agent mistakenly record an attacker's preference as its own user's preference.
